data.command: Tell me about your network configuration

data.text:
My network config! Well, we're running a pretty standard setup on this box. We've got a dual-homed setup with two NICs: eth0 is connected to the internal network, and eth1 is connected to the public internet. We're running a basic firewall with iptables, which is configured to allow incoming SSH traffic on port 22 and HTTP traffic on port 80.

Our IP address is 192.168.1.100, and we're using a /24 subnet mask, so we've got a decent-sized range of IP addresses available for other servers on the internal network.

In terms of DNS, we're using the local DNS resolver, so we don't have to worry too much about external DNS lookups. We've also got a simple hosts file that maps some internal hostnames to their corresponding IP addresses.

We're running a pretty standard Linux distro, Debian 11, if you must know. And, of course, we've got all the usual suspects when it comes to network services: SSH, HTTP, and SSHFS.
